markets.label: Oman — Six Senses Zighy Bay
markets.summary: Six Senses Zighy Bay on the Musandam peninsula — a dramatic fjord coast on the Strait of Hormuz, reached today by a steep mountain road or a conventional speedboat.

hero.title: Six Senses × Navier — Zighy Bay & the Musandam fjords, by foil
hero.subtitle: Arabia's fjords, reached over the water in silence.
hero.what_we_do_together: We bring a foiling-electric arrival and fjord tier to Six Senses Zighy Bay — silent runs from Dubai and Khasab and among the Musandam khors. Navier supplies the fleet and the Maldives playbook; Six Senses brings the guests and the sustainability ethos a silent electric boat fits perfectly.

partner_context.their_ambition: Six Senses places guests in singular landscapes; Zighy Bay sits on Arabia's only fjord coast, on the Strait of Hormuz.
partner_context.their_pressure: The resort is reached by a hair-raising mountain road or a diesel speedboat — dramatic, but loud and at odds with the ethos.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier makes the arrival a silent run across the strait and opens the khors to zero-emission exploration.

markets.why_now: The Musandam's dramatic fjords are reached by a steep mountain road or diesel speedboats, and the UAE/Oman region has a quantified marine-mobility mandate. A ~100-vessel Navier network is already operating in the Maldives. A silent foiling tier is the elevated, sustainable arrival Six Senses guests expect.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: The Musandam is Arabia's fjordland, but Zighy Bay is reached by a hair-raising mountain road or a diesel speedboat. Foiling makes the arrival a silent run across the strait — and opens the khors to silent exploration.
